messages.subject: get.resid() help
parts:
Hi Chris,

I am trying to walk-through the tutorial with an example dataset. I encountered the following error when I tried to get residuals for each group:


all.dat.resids <- lapply(groups, function(x) get.resid(lhrh[Group == x], covars=covars, exclude='Group'))
 
    Error in eval(.massagei(isub), x, parent.frame()) : 
     object 'Group' not found 

I have a 'Group' column in my covars.csv. Is there anything else that I am missing? I have attached all my input files.

Thanks in advance for your help,
Jaiashre.

messages.author: dadcb4fd6a01f8d1
messages.subject: Re: [brainGraph-help] get.resid() help
parts:
Ok, I figured it out. The code in the User Guide is out-of-date relative to newer versions of "get.resid" (for that specific section only).

1. I just want to be sure that you want to run separate linear models per group (which is where the line of code in your email is from).
As a workaround, you should do the following:
setkey(covars, Study.ID)
setkey(lhrh, Study.ID)
lhrh$Group <- covars$Group

all.dat.resids <- lapply(groups, function(x) get.resid(lhrh[Group == x, !'Group'], covars=covars[Group == x], exclude='Group'))

I will update the User Guide for this later in the week. I will probably update the function to make this type of usage easier, as well.

2. I highly recommend that you zero-pad your Study ID's, so that they will be C01, C02, etc. If you have >= 100, then it should be C001, C002, etc.
3. If you have only 10 and 5 subjects in your groups, that might be too small of a sample size for reliable results, but I am not sure. You can always try, of course.

Let me know if this worked.
Chris

messages.subject: Re: [brainGraph-help] get.resid() help
parts:
Chris,

Thank you, this worked!  I was able to follow through rest of the chapter in the guide although I made the following modifications:

1. To correlate residuals for each group separately (Section 6.5), I used:
corrs <- lapply(groups, function(x) corr.matrix(resids.all[resids.all$Group == x], densities=densities))

instead of: corrs <- lapply(groups, function(x) corr.matrix(resids.all[x], densities=densities))

2. To set graph-, vertex- and edge-level attributes (Section 6.5.2) using the below code, I had to change the column names in my input lh and rh csv files to match the 'name' in the dk atlas.
g <- Map(function(x, y) llply(x, set_brainGraph_attr, atlas=atlas, modality=modality, group=y, .progress='text'), g, as.list(groups))
But this step produced a warning message:
1: In vattrs[[name]][index] <- value :
  number of items to replace is not a multiple of replacement length
I am not sure what this means. Is this of concern?

Thank you,
Jaiashre.

messages.author: dadcb4fd6a01f8d1
messages.subject: Re: [brainGraph-help] get.resid() help
parts:
It could be a problem. What is your "atlas" variable? I see that you are using a subset of the DK atlas; so if you have done atlas='dk' then I think that is the source of the warning. I recommend instead saving only the relevant ROI's and use it as a custom atlas. You would do something along the lines of:

dk.sub <- dk[name %in% names(lhrh)[-1]]

And then use atlas='dk.sub' for subsequent function calls.
